_readme: Machine-readable expectations for the generated spec-engine corpus. See README.md. Each document declares the extraction shape a correct read of its PDF produces, and the verdicts shared/specCheck.ts must produce from it. Every expectation list is EXHAUSTIVE: an unexpected verdict is a failure just as a missing one is.

documents.title: Andersen Dairy — Certificate of Analysis, HEAVY CREAM 40%
covers: crosstab table with a laboratory control row
certification boilerplate quoting the regulation's own thresholds
reagent / plate lots carrying their own lot codes and expiry dates
a result identical to the specification printed beside it
a placeholder unit cell on a judged row
limit scope resolution — a product-pinned limit beating the tenant default

fields_must_not_contain.why: The reagent / plate lot table carries lot codes and expiry dates of its own. A 3M Petrifilm plate lot is not the product's lot, and a plate's expiry is not the product's code date. EXTRACTION-LAYER assertion — see README.

shapes.note: A correct read of the PDF. The certification paragraph's two thresholds arrive in a results table because that is what production extraction does with them.

tables.name: certification
tables.printed_verbatim_why: NOT printed as a table. This is what production extraction does to the closing certification PARAGRAPH: it lifts the regulation's two thresholds out of the prose and files them as results. The paragraph is printed; this table is the mangling of it, which is exactly the input the engine has to survive.

printed.reason_contains: the reported result is identical to the specification printed beside it, so it is a limit restated rather than a measurement
printed.message_contains: identical to the specification printed beside it

printed.reason_contains: the reported result is identical to the specification printed beside it, so it is a limit restated rather than a measurement
printed.message_contains: identical to the specification printed beside it

limit.reason_contains: the reported result is identical to the specification printed beside it, so it is a limit restated rather than a measurement
limit.message_contains: could not be judged against our limit of ≤20000 CFU/g

limit.reason_contains: the reported result is identical to the specification printed beside it, so it is a limit restated rather than a measurement
limit.message_contains: could not be judged against our limit of ≤750000

must_not.why: Buffer is the sterile negative control the lab runs beside the sample. Judging it as product is wrong in both directions, and a reviewer taught to wave off 'that's just the buffer' will wave off the real failure sitting next to it.
Nothing in the control row may be judged, whatever its label was read as.
100,000 is the regulation's standard-plate-count threshold quoted in the certification paragraph. Nothing was measured; it must never surface as a measured value.
400,000 is the regulation's somatic-cell threshold. Same argument.
The certification rows are boilerplate. They may be reported as not_checked, never graded — an out_of_spec here is a fabricated alert on a supplier already under scrutiny.
And never as a pass either: a pass would assert the document certified something it only quoted.
The reagent / plate lot table is not test results and must yield nothing at all.
'Coliform Count Plate (CC)' is a 3M consumable, not an analyte. A looser name match would judge a plate as a coliform result.
Heavy cream's fat must be judged against the product-pinned 38-42% limit, not the tenant-wide 30-35% default that would call 40.12% a failure.

documents.title: Cascade Analytical Services — micro + chemical report, cream cheese spread
covers: a long table with printed Specification and Pass/Fail columns
the document contradicting itself — value outside its own printed range, row marked Pass
scientific notation with the unit in its own column (2x10^3, 1.2e3)
a censored value that straddles our limit (<50 vs 10) and one that clears it (<1 vs 10)
MPN units, which are not CFU
the absence vocabulary labs print: Negative, Not Detected, Non-detectable for ... /25g, Absent/25g
placeholder unit cells: N/A, none, an em dash
a percent value judged against a percent limit
a percent refused against a CFU limit (misextraction shape)

fields_must_not_contain.why: The report number, the accreditation certificate and the analytical method codes are identifiers, not lots. EXTRACTION-LAYER assertion.

shapes.note: A correct read of the PDF.

printed.reason_contains: reported as <1, which cannot confirm absence

limit.reason_contains: reported as <50, which straddles the 10 limit — the true value could fall either side
limit.message_contains: could not be judged against our limit of ≤10 CFU/g

limit.reason_contains: result is in MPN/g but the limit is in CFU/g — not comparable
limit.message_contains: could not be judged against our limit of ≤10 CFU/g

limit.reason_contains: reported as <1, which cannot confirm absence

must_not.why: 2×10³ is 2000, not 2. Reading the leading token made a value twice its printed ceiling look like a comfortable pass — the worst class of bug this engine can have.
<50 against our 10 limit is not a pass. The true value could be 2 or 49, and calling it in spec is the false negative that discredits the feature.
...and it is not a failure either. Both answers are lies; the honest one is not_checked.
MPN and CFU are different enumeration methods. A 3.0 MPN/g result must never be graded against a CFU/g limit in either direction.
Same row, same argument, other direction.
'Non-detectable for Listeria mono/25g' is the pathogen result that matters most. It must be read, and it must not read as a failure.

A placeholder unit cell means the row carries no unit — the same statement as a blank. Treating 'none' or '—' as a unit in its own right makes it mismatch every real unit and refuses rows that were perfectly judgeable.
'Pass' in a disposition column is the document asserting its own compliance, never a measurement.

shapes.note: The PDF prints a clean chemical block. This shape is what production extraction did to one (prod document '100/1OZ CUP CREAM CH SPRD - RASKAS'): a micro specification misfiled onto the chemical rows. The engine cannot fix a misread — it can only refuse to grade across it, which is what this pins. Both forms are here: a percent in its own unit column, and a percent carried on the value.

tables.name: chemical_physical_analysis
tables.printed_verbatim_why: NOT printed. The PDF prints a clean chemical block; this is the observed misextraction (a micro specification misfiled onto chemical rows) that the engine must refuse to grade across.

printed.reason_contains: result is in % but the limit is in CFU/g — not comparable
result is in % but the limit is in CFU/g — not comparable

must_not.why: A percent and a count are incomparable. Compared, 33.09% reads as three times a 10 CFU/g ceiling and the reviewer gets a fabricated alert; refused, they get the truth.
And never a silent pass either.

documents.title: NorthStar Creamery — fluid dairy COA, per mL and per g on one certificate
covers: CFU/mL results against CFU/g limits — refused by default
the same analyte printed per mL on one line and per g on another
the per-tenant unit-equivalence setting flipping a verdict, and announcing that it did
rows whose units lined up on their own carrying no equivalence note

fields_must_not_contain.why: 41-118 is the plant number and 4.2 is a QA policy reference. EXTRACTION-LAYER assertion.

shapes.note: The tenant has said nothing about units. The per-millilitre majority of this certificate is judged against nothing at all, and says so.

limit.reason_contains: result is in CFU/mL but the limit is in CFU/g — not comparable
limit.message_contains: could not be judged against our limit of ≤10 CFU/g

limit.reason_contains: result is in CFU/mL but the limit is in CFU/g — not comparable

must_not.why: CFU/mL against a CFU/g limit is a genuinely different quantity for a powder. Off by default means off — no verdict may be graded across the bases.
Same row, other direction.
Nothing here was equated, so nothing may claim it was.

shapes.note: The same document with the tenant's volume/mass equivalence ON. Row 0 flips from not_checked to out_of_spec — the one setting in this engine that can change a verdict, and every verdict it made reachable names it.

limit.reason_contains: 120 exceeds the 10 limit (CFU/mL judged as CFU/g, per this tenant's setting)
limit.message_contains: outside our limit of ≤10 CFU/g (CFU/mL judged as CFU/g, per this tenant's setting)

limit.reason_contains: 4500 is within the 20000 limit (CFU/mL judged as CFU/g, per this tenant's setting)
limit.message_contains: within our limit of ≤20000 CFU/g (CFU/mL judged as CFU/g, per this tenant's setting)

must_not.why: The two per-gram rows lined up on their own. Marking them as equated would be a lie about rows that never needed the setting.
Same, the other per-gram row.

documents.title: Valley Co-Pack — one certificate, three products, three lots
covers: a multi-product certificate that historically collapsed into one record
a result the supplier passed and our tighter limit fails
a placeholder unit column on a micro row that must still be judged
scientific notation beside a placeholder unit

fields_must_not_contain.why: 18449271604 is the FDA facility registration on the letterhead, not a lot. EXTRACTION-LAYER assertion.

shapes.note: Three scopes, one per item block. A single-scope read is the historic multi-record collapse and would lose two lots and the failure each carries.

must_not.why: Item 2's coliform is inside the supplier's own printed ceiling. Their paper is not wrong; our limit is tighter. The printed source must stay silent about it.
A unit cell reading 'N/A' means the row carries no unit. Refusing it would drop a genuine 4x-over-limit coliform result, which was 45 of the 74 unjudgeable rows in a 100-COA production sample.

documents.title: Andersen Dairy — Continuing Guaranty (not a COA)
covers: a non-COA document that must produce no spec results at all

fields_must_not_contain.why: Statute sections, a tolerance figure and a facility registration are not lots, products or expirations. EXTRACTION-LAYER assertion.

shapes.note: The signature block extracts as a key/value table, which is the harder case: the engine has a 'result' column to find and must still produce nothing.

tables.name: guaranty_details
rows: Medosweet Farms, Inc., 1150 Central Ave N, Kent, WA 98032
tables.printed_verbatim_why: NOT printed as a table. The guaranty is prose plus a signature block; this is a plausible extractor synthesis of it, used here to prove that even when a non-COA hands the engine a result column it produces nothing.

must_not.why: A legal guaranty contains no test results. A spec engine that finds one here will invent them anywhere.
